blocks.label: SHORTEST PART HOLDING A, B AND C?

slides.teaser: The problem, as a shelf of jars
slides.title: A recipe run
slides.scene: A recipe needs one A, one B and one C. Walk along the jars, grab until you hold all three, then put jars back from the left while you still do.

blocks.text: B C A holds all three. What is the shortest stretch that does?

slides.title: LeetCode 76
slides.lead: Return the shortest part of s that holds every letter of t, repeats included.

blocks.text: LeetCode's own example: ADOBECODEBANC with ABC gives {{LEET}}.
s and t hold up to 100,000 letters. No answer: return "".

slides.try_first: Find the shortest stretch of ABDBCA holding A, B and C by hand.

slides.title: Grow, then shrink
slides.lead: Post 08's window: grow the right end until every letter is inside, then shrink from the left.

blocks.label: FIRST WINDOW WITH ALL THREE
blocks.note: A B D B C holds A, B and C. Now try dropping from the left.

slides.title: Count what's needed
slides.lead: Post 05's map: need[c] is how many more of letter c the window still lacks.

blocks.text: A letter joining lowers its need; leaving raises it.

slides.title: One number: missing
slides.lead: missing = letters of t not covered yet. Lower it only when need[c] was above 0.

blocks.label: THE SECOND B
blocks.text: need[B] is already 0, so the extra B is [[not progress]]: missing stays 1.

slides.title: Record, then shrink
slides.lead: While missing is 0, record the window, then drop the left letter.

slides.title: Watch it search
slides.lead: Grow and shrink on ABDBCA, looking for A, B and C.

final.caption: {{BEST}}: 3 letters with A, B and C.

lines: return s from bestStart, bestLen letters

items.label: Time
items.note: Each letter joins once, leaves once.

slides.pattern: Grow until nothing is missing, then shrink while nothing is.

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.note: Same need and missing, with a fixed-size window.

blog.summary: The shortest stretch that holds every letter of t: grow until nothing is missing, then shrink.
blog.tested_what: The grow-and-shrink window with need and missing
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the LeetCode examples, no answer, t longer than s, repeated letters in t) and random strings of up to 12 letters from 2 to 4 letters, plus one string of 400 letters
blog.tested_against: a brute force that tries every stretch from the shortest up
blog.tested_extra: The walk, the answer and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: LeetCode 76 Minimum Window Substring solved with hints: a sliding window plus need and missing counts.
lines: Grow until nothing is missing, record, then shrink while nothing is.
The trap: lower missing for every letter and ABDBCA returns "{{WRONG}}".
